name: Samarth- Empowering lives through clean technology
description: Udaipur Urja Initiatives Producer Company Limited is a producer company, incorporated and registered in 2014 in the Udaipur district of the state of Rajasthan in India working in the twin verticals of clean technology and agriculture. The project activity will encompass the following activity- replacement of traditional cookstoves used by communities with technologically advanced cookstoves having low emissions and high thermal efficiency. The project will be implemented in the rural areas of southern Rajasthan. Implementation of the project depends on the successful validation and registration of the project as a CDM project activity since the project will be financed completely from carbon revenues. The proposed improved cookstoves project will be implemented with the financial support of carbon revenue under the Gold Standard for Global Goals (GS4GG)
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: GS TPDDTEC V4.0: REDUCED EMISSIONS FROM COOKING AND HEATING – TECHNOLOGIES AND PRACTICES TO DISPLACE DECENTRALIZED THERMAL ENERGY CONSUMPTION

name: Shilichong AMWS GHG Mitigation Project
description: Shilichong AMWS GHG Mitigation Project installs new animal waste management system (AWMS) to an existing swine farm in Chaling County, which is owned by Chaling Longhua Ecological Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The biogas generated during the treatment process is captured for power generation and surplus biogas is destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The total installed capacity of the proposed project is 6.0MW and the annual electricity production is estimated to be 39,222MWh. After anaerobic digestion, the sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the separated solid and the effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: ACM0010 GHG emission reductions from manure management systems

name: Salkhit wind farm
description:
Clean Energy LLC has a wind farm in the area called Salkhit uul 70 km southeast of Mongolia’s capital, Ulaanbaatar. The wind farm has a capacity of 49.6 MW and generates 168.5 GWh of electricity per year.
The Salkhit wind farm began commercial operation on 25/06/2013. It generates renewable electricity using wind resources and sells the output to the Central Energy System based on a power purchase agreement. It is the first grid-connected wind farm in Mongolia, aiming to lead the country’s renewable energy development. By supplying clean electricity to the grid, it avoids CO2 emissions from fossil fuel power plants.
The project consists of 31 wind turbines with a total capacity of 50 MW, supplying 164 GWh annually to the grid. According to ACM0002, the project qualifies as a renewable electricity activity. The baseline scenario is the supply of the same amount of electricity by the grid, as prior to project implementation.
The project boundary includes the site and all power plants physically connected to the grid.
Given that the grid is primarily powered by thermal plants, the project contributes to significant GHG emission reductions. For the second crediting period (24/06/2020 to 23/06/2027), estimated reductions total 1,332,835 tCO2e, with an annual average of 190,405 tCO2e.As Mongolia’s first wind farm, it helps commercialize renewable technologies, improve air quality, reduce pollutants like SO₂ and soot, and create local jobs during construction and operation.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
